solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: What nude model has, compared to topless one? Class

definitions.text: What nude model has, compared to topless one?
definitions.meaning: a model wearing nothing has fewer clothes on than one who is merely bare above the waist
a period of teaching in school

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as two words for the first reading: a nude model has 'less on' than a topless one.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a class or period of teaching at school is also called by this word.

clue.text: Slacker's shoe

definitions.meaning: an idle person who lounges about
a slip-on casual shoe without laces

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: an idler who lounges about, and a laceless slip-on moccasin-style shoe.

clue.text: Mad sniper injured fictional hero

indicators.note: something injured is damaged and out of shape, so the letters of the two words before it are reformed

explanation.surface: A deranged gunman has wounded a hero from the comics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injured' tells you to rearrange MAD SNIPER.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the web-slinging comic-book character created by Stan Lee is a fictional superhero.

clue.text: Wayward golfers might do this greeting in Open

indicators.note: the greeting is placed in the middle of the word for open

parts.note: overt means open, not concealed
hi is a casual greeting

explanation.surface: Golfers who stray off line might shout a hello at the Open championship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open' looks like the golf championship but is just the adjective meaning not hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: a golfer who strikes the ball too hard sends it past the target, which explains wayward shots.

clue.text: In my view, idiot's not given justice, when stalking a relative

indicators.note: the trimmed idiot follows behind the relative, as a stalker trails someone

parts.note: sis is short for sister, a relative

indicators.note: the abbreviation for justice is withheld from the word for idiot

parts.note: eejit is an Irish and Scottish word for an idiot
J is the abbreviation for Justice, as in a judge's title

explanation.surface: Someone opines that a fool was denied a fair hearing while following a family member about.
explanation.walkthrough: EEJIT is the Irish spelling of idiot; without J it gives EEIT. 'when' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: the four-word phrase introduces a personal opinion, just like 'in my view'.

clue.text: Second research centre for chocolate bar?

parts.note: a lab, or laboratory, is a centre for research

explanation.surface: A query whether a second laboratory is being set up to study confectionery.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose example: a thick flat block of chocolate is sold as one of these, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Prison officer finally lifted loop

parts.note: stir is slang for prison

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of officer

parts.note: lifted means raised up

explanation.surface: A prison warder was eventually hoisted up by a noose.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: the rider's foot rests in a metal loop hanging from the saddle.

clue.text: In centre of Cape Town, police brought back order

indicators.note: the reversed police go in the middle of the centre letters
the central pair of letters of the place name taken as one word
brought back means the letters for the police are read the other way

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of the British police

explanation.surface: In central Cape Town, the police restored order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of' treats Cape Town as one word, whose middle pair is ET; 'brought back' gives DIC, placed 'In' that pair. The surface's police in South Africa are a distraction.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a decree or official command issued by an authority is an order.

clue.text: Fabricated residence, to vagrant, had everything

indicators.note: vagrant means wandering, so the letters around it wander into a new order

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: A made-up home, says the tramp, had it all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vagrant' makes ADH; the comma suggests a tramp speaking, but 'to' simply stays as it is.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: Mr Toad's grand home in The Wind in the Willows is a fictional residence.

clue.text: Adverse tone Sir Alex partly developed

indicators.note: read cryptically as averse or turned away, so the letters run backwards
partly says only some of the letters of these words are used

explanation.surface: A hostile tone from Sir Alex Ferguson partly came about.
explanation.walkthrough: Hidden in 'toNE SIR Alex' is NESIRA, which 'Adverse' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: something that has come up or emerged has developed.

clue.text: Classical building leaves one cold — amateur!

parts.note: basil is a herb whose leaves are used in cooking
I is the Roman numeral one
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A remark that a classical structure leaves somebody cold, with a jibe of 'amateur!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like a verb but is the herb whose leaves are eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a Roman oblong hall with an apse, later the form of many churches.

clue.text: One doesn't forget medical department obtaining help moving American

indicators.note: the hospital department takes in the shuffled letters, holding them

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

indicators.note: moving suggests the letters shift around

explanation.surface: A patient remembers a hospital department fetching help to move an American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' makes LEPHA, which the department is 'obtaining'. 'One doesn't forget' alludes to the saying that these animals never forget.
explanation.definitionFit: A proverb: these big beasts are said never to forget.

clue.text: Mark's regularly enraged by four-by-four vehicle reversing

indicators.note: regularly means take every other letter of enraged
reversing turns round the letters of the vehicle

parts.note: an SUV is a sport utility vehicle, a four-by-four

explanation.surface: A man called Mark keeps getting angry at a big off-roader backing up.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of 'enraged' give NAE; 'reversing' turns SUV into VUS. 'Mark's' reads as Mark is.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a birthmark or mole on the skin is a mark, the medical term.

clue.text: Staff check follows constant routine

indicators.note: the chess abbreviation comes after the other pieces

parts.note: C is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
a rut is a dull routine
CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: An inspection of staff comes after a constant routine.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a walking support stick or prop for the lame is a staff.

clue.text: Musical piece, with beat elevated in much of 'Neighbours', say

indicators.note: the raised beat sits in the trimmed soap opera
much of means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Neighbours is an Australian soap opera, popular in Britain

indicators.note: elevated in a down clue means the word is read upwards

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them

explanation.surface: A tune with its beat raised features in most episodes of a TV show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'much of' drops the final letter, 'elevated' gives NAT, set 'in' the rest. Neighbours is an Australian TV soap opera long shown in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a composition for one or two instruments in several movements is a musical piece.

clue.text: Part of shell found by the roofer working with lamp

indicators.note: working suggests letters being worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A seashell fragment turned up by a roofer using a lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges THE ROOFER with LAMP; 'found by' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: nacre, the iridescent inner layer of some molluscs' shells, goes by this name.

clue.text: Citadel 25 mounted, applying gloss briefly

indicators.note: mounted in a down clue means the word reads upwards

parts.note: the solution to 25 down, a killer whale

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, losing the final letter

parts.note: to polish is to apply a gloss to something

explanation.surface: A fortress with a mounted whale given a quick shine.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 25 is ORCA, turned upward as ACRO; POLISH loses its end to give POLIS.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the Athenian hilltop fortress with the Parthenon is the most famous citadel of this kind.

clue.text: Mirror raised, holding edge with uncertainty that is short-lived

indicators.note: the turned mimic holds the other pieces inside it
raised in a down clue means the word reads upwards

parts.note: to ape is to mirror or copy
a hem is the edge of cloth
er is a hesitant sound expressing uncertainty

explanation.surface: A mirror is lifted, its rim held uncertainly, and soon gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' gives EPA, 'holding' the edge and the hesitation. 'Mirror' reads as a noun but is the verb to copy.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: collectible items made to last a day, such as tickets and posters, are things of brief life.

clue.text: Prison urinals derelict, bringing about bitter hostility

definitions.text: Prison urinals derelict, bringing about bitter hostility

parts.note: pen is a slang word for prison, short for penitentiary

indicators.note: derelict means ruined, so these letters fall into a new order

parts.note: war is bitter hostility between parties

explanation.surface: Run-down jail toilets provoking a fierce conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'derelict' turns URINALS into INSULAR. The whole clue also describes the conflict, so it reads as a description of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the 1807-1814 conflict in Spain and Portugal against Napoleon was a long and bitter one.

clue.text: Goddess is seen amongst Home Counties chaps — on the rebound?

indicators.note: bouncing back suggests the letters are read backwards
the little word is seen in among the letters of the region

parts.note: SE, the South East of England, where the counties around London lie
men are chaps

explanation.surface: A goddess is seen among Home Counties men, recovering from a failed romance.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties around London in South East England. 'seen amongst' places the little word inside, and 'on the rebound' gives the reading backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the Greek deity of retribution who punished arrogance was a goddess.

clue.text: Shrewd hosts, acting vacuously, cook in an eccentric style

indicators.note: the shrewd word plays host to the pieces inside it

parts.note: wily means shrewd or cunning
A is an abbreviation for acting, as in a temporary rank

indicators.note: emptied of its middle, leaving only the outer letters of cook

explanation.surface: Clever party hosts, acting vacantly, cook oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacuously' empties the word for cook to its outer letters, CK, and the shrewd word 'hosts' that pair with the A.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: doing something wackily is behaving in a zany, oddball way.

clue.text: Playing partners canoodle, turning up under the first arch

indicators.note: in a down clue the later pieces sit below the first

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, the first
North and South are partners at the bridge table

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue reverses the word

parts.note: to pet is to canoodle

explanation.surface: Partners in a game kiss and cuddle, turning up beneath the first archway.
explanation.walkthrough: N and S are partners in bridge; 'turning up' reverses PET to TEP.
explanation.definitionFit: A part of the foot: the arched middle section between toes and ankle bears this name.

clue.text: Bury Market latterly governed by single retired doctor

indicators.note: the last letter is controlled by the turned word around it
retired means drawn back, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: single means one

indicators.note: latterly picks the last letter of market

parts.note: MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: The market in Bury, a Lancashire town, ruled by a lone retired doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is a town near Manchester, misleading as a place. ONE retired gives ENO, round T.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to bury someone is to lay the body in a tomb.

clue.text: Flash partner of A. Lloyd Webber

definitions.meaning: a flash is an instant, a very short moment
the lyricist Tim Rice, styled with an initial just as the composer is

explanation.walkthrough: Tim Rice wrote lyrics for Lloyd Webber's musicals; written with an initial like 'A. Lloyd Webber' he becomes T. Rice.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an instant, as in 'in a flash', means a very short time.

clue.text: What cheek to criticise kitchen help?

parts.note: sauce is cheek or impudence
to pan is to criticise harshly

explanation.surface: An outraged reaction to someone criticising the kitchen staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kitchen help' looks like a cook's assistant but is a cooking utensil, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A whimsical example: a cooking pot with a long handle is a helpful kitchen item.

clue.text: Ocean dweller, wanting either NY (Atlantic) ____ (Pacific)?

parts.note: either ... or: the missing word between the two states is or
CA, California, is the state on the Pacific coast, as NY is on the Atlantic

explanation.surface: A puzzle over which coast a sea creature lives on, New York's or the West Coast.
explanation.walkthrough: The blank is filled with 'or CA', so the phrase reads NY or CA: New York (Atlantic) or California (Pacific).
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the killer whale is a large marine mammal living in the ocean.

clue.text: Government official's recording company clown misdirecting trains

parts.note: EMI is a British record company

indicators.note: sending it the wrong way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: an ass is a fool or clown
RY is an abbreviation for railway, which runs trains

explanation.surface: An official's record label has a clown sending trains the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misdirecting' turns ASS backwards into SSA.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an envoy sent on a government's behalf is an official representative.

clue.text: Dicky in punt gets allocated berth

indicators.note: the sick word goes in the middle of the wager

parts.note: a punt is a bet
dicky is British slang for unwell or weak, as in a dicky heart

explanation.surface: A man called Dicky, in a punt, is given a mooring place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a name; it is British slang for poorly, ILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: soldiers' assigned lodgings or a sleeping place assigned to someone.

clue.text: Yankee's half-exposed fraud here in the Chilterns

indicators.note: half of the word is stripped off, leaving its first four letters

parts.note: a Yankee is an American
a sham is a fraud

explanation.surface: An American's partly revealed swindle took place in the Chiltern Hills.
explanation.walkthrough: AMERICAN loses its second half. The Chilterns are chalk hills north-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a Buckinghamshire market town lying in the Chiltern Hills.

clue.text: Sally's outside in rich habitat, cutting back plant

indicators.note: going back means the letters are read in reverse
the outer letters of the name are put in the middle of the smart word

parts.note: posh means smart and upper-class, the setting of the rich

indicators.note: the outside letters of Sally, its first and last

explanation.surface: Sally is outside in a wealthy setting, pruning a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' gives SY, put 'in' the smart word, and 'cutting back' gives the reverse. The 's of Sally's reads as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a fragrant herb of the mint family used in medicine and cooking.
